hero.title: 🛡️ Fortress Name Generator
hero.tagline: Bastions, fastnesses, orc stockades and border forts, from Oathwall to Fortress World Keldris.

article.intro: Good fortress names sound like they'll never fall: Dawnward, Kaldnar Fastness, Fort Steadfast. A castle is a home with walls, but a fortress exists to hold the line. This **fortress name generator** builds names for heroic bastions, dwarven fastnesses, orc strongholds, dark citadels, frontier forts and sci-fi fortress worlds, with an optional line of history for your campaign.

sections.heading: Eight good fortress names
sections.content:
All eight came from the generator, across its six styles:

  • Dawnward: a one-word name for a fortress that faces the enemy at sunrise.
  • Vigilgate, where the paladins train their squires: a heroic fortress with a purpose.
  • Kaldnar Fastness, that held out against goblins for forty winters: a dwarven stronghold with a reputation.
  • Kragzug, whose chieftain wears a crown made of a cooking pot: an orc stronghold with a sense of humour.
  • The Smouldering Bulwark, its gates carved with the faces of the conquered: a dark fortress you don't want to visit.
  • Fort Ashwell, manned by twelve soldiers and a very old dog: a frontier fort that's barely holding on.
  • Fort Hawk Ridge, its commander a disgraced knight with something to prove: a frontier post with a ready-made NPC.
  • Redoubt Theta, commanded by an AI that has never slept: a sci-fi fortress with a military code name.

sections.heading: How fortresses got their names
sections.content:
Many British place names began as fortifications. Alfred the Great built a network of burhs, fortified towns, against the Vikings, and the Old English burh survives in endings like -bury and -borough. Older still, the Roman castra, a military camp, gave English the -chester, -caster and -cester of Chester, Lancaster and Leicester. Before both, Iron Age people built hillforts like Maiden Castle in Dorset, one of the largest in Britain.

  • Fantasy fortresses use words for holding the line: ward, wall, gate, bulwark, redoubt.
  • Dwarven ones are fastnesses, an old word for a stronghold, cut into the rock.
  • Orcish strongholds are named for what's nailed to the gate: Three Skulls Stronghold.
  • Dark fortresses are citadels of ash and doom.
  • Frontier forts are stockades, blockhouses and lookouts named for the nearest landmark.
  • Sci-fi fortresses take code names with Greek letters: Sentinel Lambda.

Choose With a line of history for something worth knowing about it, from its armoury to its commander.

sections.heading: Using a fortress in your campaign
sections.content:
• Ask what it guards. A pass, a ford, a border or a secret: the answer shapes the name.
  • Give it a siege. A fortress that held for forty winters has veterans and ghosts.
  • Fortress or castle? If a family lives in it, it's a castle. If an army does, it's a fortress.

For a home with walls, try the Castle Name Generator, and for what's underneath, the Dungeon Name Generator. Dwarven and orcish fortresses pair with the Dwarf City and Orc Stronghold name generators, and a fallen fortress with the Ruins Name Generator.

For more, see all the world-building name generators.

faqs.question: What are good fortress names?
faqs.answer: Names about holding the line: Dawnward, Vigilgate, Kaldnar Fastness or Fort Steadfast. Choose a style for dwarven, orcish, dark, frontier or sci-fi fortresses.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a fortress and a castle?
faqs.answer: A castle is a fortified home, usually a lord's. A fortress is built for war and garrisoned by soldiers, and may have no lord living in it at all.

faqs.question: What is a fastness?
faqs.answer: An old word for a stronghold, a place made secure. It suits dwarven holds cut deep into a mountain.
